findings.message: The new reason codes make the server authoritative for the Italy/non-Italy housing-kind split (ItalyMhi / NonItalyMha), but the table still derives every other Italy-dependent decision from the client-side country === 'IT' guess in getHousingKind. The two can disagree, so a user whose mhaEit code is ItalyMhi but whose staffInfo.country is not IT is told 'Must complete an MHI form instead' while the MHI rows and the paper-MHI note are both suppressed — an instruction with no way to act on it.
findings.evidence: eligibilityReasons.ts trusts reasonCode first and only falls back to getHousingKind; EligibilityStatusTable.tsx:78-80 showMhiRows and :132/:140 the MHI Eligibility cells still use getHousingKind(country) alone. The new test case (EligibilityStatusTable.test.tsx, userCountry='US' + ItalyMhi) renders exactly this mismatched state and asserts it, per its own comment: 'the ItalyMhi row also proves the API code takes precedence over the country-based guess'.
findings.recommendation: Pick one owner for the housing-kind fact. Either derive showMhiRows/the paper-form note from the reason code too (ItalyMhi implies MHI applies), or keep the country as the sole authority and treat the code as reason copy only. Leaving country authoritative for row visibility while the code is authoritative for row text lets the table point a user at a form whose section it just hid.
findings.fix: Compute one code-aware `kind` per person in housingAllowance.ts and feed both showMhiRows and the reason lookups from it, instead of mixing getHousingKind with reasonCode precedence.

findings.message: Both reason maps are typed as a full Record<MinistersHousingIneligibilityReasonEnum, string> over an API-generated enum, so the next backend-added reason code breaks the TypeScript build even though the runtime already degrades gracefully. The repo rule for this tree requires Partial<Record<ApiEnum, T>> plus a runtime fallback precisely because these enums are in flux.
findings.evidence: codegen.ts builds src/graphql/types.generated.ts from `schema = [apiUrl, ...]` (the live API), so MinistersHousingIneligibilityReasonEnum regenerates on every `yarn gql`; a new member makes both full Records incomplete. Lines 445 and 497 declare `Record<MinistersHousingIneligibilityReasonEnum, string>`, while line 479 already has `reasonCopy[reasonCode ?? fallbackCode] ?? reasonCopy[fallbackCode]` to handle a code this client does not know.
findings.recommendation: Type both maps as Partial<Record<MinistersHousingIneligibilityReasonEnum, string>> and keep the existing `?? reasonCopy[fallbackCode]` as the runtime fallback. That preserves the intended behaviour for unknown codes (the comment on lines 474-478 already states this is the goal) without coupling compilation to the backend enum, and lets the two deliberately-unreachable NonItalyMha / ItalyMhi placeholder entries be dropped rather than mapped to misleading copy.
findings.fix: Change both `const reasonCopy: Record<MinistersHousingIneligibilityReasonEnum, string>` declarations to `Partial<Record<MinistersHousingIneligibilityReasonEnum, string>>`.

findings.message: This call site drops the `hasSpouse ? … : undefined` gating on every spouse prop while the only other call site of the same shared component keeps the equivalent `isMarried ?` gating on all of them. The two consumers now follow opposite conventions for the same six spouse props.
findings.evidence: MhaRequestSection.tsx passes spouseEligible/spouseCountry/spouseMhiEligibility ungated; MinisterHousingAllowance.tsx:162-191 still gates spouseEligible, spouseCountry, spouseMhiEligibility and both new reason codes on isMarried.
findings.recommendation: The ungating is behavior-neutral here — SalaryCalculatorContext.tsx:113/126 sets hcmSpouse to null exactly when hasSpouse is false — but divergence across the only two consumers makes the spouse contract ambiguous. Either make the component the single gate (documenting that spousePreferredName is the switch) and ungate both call sites, or keep both gated.
findings.fix: Ungate the spouse props in MinisterHousingAllowance.tsx the same way, or restore the hasSpouse gate here; pick one and state the rule on the props interface.

findings.message: getIneligibilityReason maps the NonItalyMha code to 'Not applicable', which defeats the graceful fallback the function is built around: an unrecognized code degrades to the country-based guess, but this known-yet-inapplicable code renders 'Not applicable' in the Reason cell of a row whose Eligibility cell reads 'Ineligible'.
findings.evidence: `[MinistersHousingIneligibilityReasonEnum.NonItalyMha]: t('Not applicable')` sits in the MHA map annotated 'Unreachable in MHA results', while the return below handles unknown codes via `?? reasonCopy[fallbackCode]`.
findings.recommendation: The Record is exhaustive by type so some value is required, but the safe value for a code that should never reach this map is the country-based fallback copy, not a dead end. That keeps one degradation path for every code this client cannot meaningfully explain.
findings.fix: Map NonItalyMha in the MHA record to the same copy as NoIbsCertification (or route it through fallbackCode) rather than 'Not applicable'.

findings.message: Several map entries are commented "Unreachable" (e.g. NonItalyMha in MHA results, ItalyMhi in MHI results) based on an assumption about what the backend can send, but nothing enforces or tests that invariant — if the API ever does send one of these combinations, the UI would silently show a misleading "Not applicable" or wrong-category message with no test to catch it.
findings.evidence: eligibilityReasons.ts: "Unreachable in MHA results (the MHA country check only fails for Italy)" and "Unreachable in MHI results: Italy staff pass the MHI country check" — both assumptions live only in comments, not in a runtime assertion or test.
findings.recommendation: Either narrow the parameter type so the "unreachable" members cannot be passed, or add a test documenting what the UI shows if the assumption is violated, so a future API change surfaces as a test failure rather than a silent bad label.
findings.fix: No mechanical fix; requires a design decision on how to encode the invariant.

findings.message: The fallback branch for an ineligibility reason code the client does not recognize (e.g. a new enum value the API ships before this client redeploys) is never exercised by a test — only the null-code fallback is covered.
findings.evidence: getIneligibilityReason/getMhiReason: `return reasonCopy[reasonCode ?? fallbackCode] ?? reasonCopy[fallbackCode];` — the `?? reasonCopy[fallbackCode]` branch (reasonCode present but missing from the map) has no corresponding it.each case; all new tests pass either a mapped enum member or omit the prop entirely.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that casts an unrecognized string as the enum type (or a similar simulated unknown value) and asserts the fallback copy is shown, to lock in the documented "newer than this client" behavior.
findings.fix: it('falls back for an unrecognized reason code', () => render with userIneligibilityReasonCode cast to an unknown string, assert fallback text)

findings.message: EligibilityStatusTable grows to 12 parallel user*/spouse* scalar props (six matched pairs), so every added facet costs two props plus two threading sites in each consumer. The shape invites exactly the per-person/per-kind pairing mistakes this diff had to thread carefully.
findings.evidence: Props now span userPreferredName/userEligible/userCountry/userMhiEligibility/userIneligibilityReasonCode/userMhiIneligibilityReasonCode plus the identical spouse* set.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to a per-person object (preferredName, eligible, country, mhiEligibility, ineligibilityReasonCode, mhiIneligibilityReasonCode) with `user` plus optional `spouse`. The component already treats spouse presence as one switch and useMhaRequestData already builds both sides in one place, so the change is local to two call sites.
findings.fix: Introduce an `EligibilityPerson` interface and change the props to `{ user: EligibilityPerson; spouse?: EligibilityPerson; compact?: boolean }`.
